title: The Nazca Lines Mystery
hook: In the early 20th century, pilots first reported seeing giant desert drawings in Peru that still puzzle researchers.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: In 1940, a Peruvian pilot reported spotting giant lines from the sky over Nazca.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: The geoglyphs include a hummingbird about 93 m long, a spider about 47 m, and a monkey about 93 m long, created sometime between 500 BC and 500 AD.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Researchers using satellite imagery in 2015 identified hundreds of figures, some only visible from high altitude.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Archaeologists suggest the lines may be linked to an ancient culture such as Paracas, involving removal of surface material to expose lighter soil.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: One theory proposes the figures served as astronomical markers aligned with solstice sunrise.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Recent lidar scans in 2022 revealed hidden lines beneath the surface, suggesting the site is far more extensive than previously thought.

end.line: What purpose could these massive desert drawings truly serve?

description: Exploring the mysterious Nazca Lines and the clues that keep researchers guessing.

facts.claim: In 1940, Peruvian pilot Juan Pablo Cueva first reported the Nazca Lines from the air
The Nazca geoglyphs include a hummingbird, spider and a 370-meter long monkey dating to around 500 BC
Satellite imagery in 2015 confirmed over 300 geoglyphs, many only visible from high altitude
Archaeologists associate the lines with the Paracas culture (c. 800-100 BC) using stone removal technique
Lidar surveys in 2022 uncovered previously unknown lines beneath the surface
